chunks: Ali ibn Isa al-Mujawir, who lived near the Kufa Mosque, may God be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Isma'il ibn Ali ibn Razin, the brother of Da'b al ibn Ali al-Khuza'i, narrated to us. He said: Da'b al ibn Ali narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Hasan Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) narrated to me, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him).

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There are four groups on whose behalf I will intercede on the Day of Resurrection: Those who honor my offspring after me; those who fulfill their needs; those who strive to assist them in their affairs when they have need of him; and those who love them with their hearts and their tongues.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the four groups for whom the Prophet will intercede on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the lineage of Imam Musa al-Ridha, highlights the Shia concept of *shafa'ah* (intercession) as a divine privilege granted to those who maintain strong spiritual and practical ties to the Ahl al-Bayt. It underscores the importance of both internal devotion (*muhibbin*) and external service (*saa'in*) to the Imams, reflecting the dual nature of leadership in Shia theology where spiritual love is validated by active support. The inclusion of al-Ridha in the chain emphasizes the continuity of this tradition from the Prophet through the Twelve Imams.
